In LaTeX, the `\rowcolor` command is used to change the background color of a row in a table. This command is part of the `colortbl` package, so you'll first need to include this package in your document preamble. Here's a basic example of how to use `\rowcolor`:

```latex
\documentclass{article}
\usepackage{colortbl} % Required for \rowcolor
\usepackage{xcolor}   % Required for color definitions

\begin{document}

\begin{tabular}{|l|c|r|}
\hline
\rowcolor{gray!20} % Light gray background
Header 1 & Header 2 & Header 3 \\
\hline
Data 1 & Data 2 & Data 3 \\
\rowcolor{blue!10} % Light blue background
Data 4 & Data 5 & Data 6 \\
Data 7 & Data 8 & Data 9 \\
\hline
\end{tabular}

\end{document}
```

### Explanation:
- First, you need to use the `colortbl` package to enable the use of `\rowcolor`.
- The `xcolor` package is used to define colors. You can specify colors by name or mix your colors using models like `rgb`, `CMYK`, or other predefined names.
- The `\rowcolor{<color>}` command changes the background color of the row immediately following it.
- Colors can have an intensity specified by a percentage in the form of `[colorname!percentage]`.

You can replace `gray!20` or `blue!10` with any valid color name or percentage to achieve the desired effect.
